note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BAH 6(1)(a); A06b BAH 6(1)(a); L05 BAH 9(1)(a), 7(1); BAH 8(c), 7(2)): ordinary naturalisation after 25 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from the father only, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Bahrain, 2024
sources.said: Person has resided in the country for 25 years. ... n.a. ... Person has voluntarily acquired another citizenship without prior permission and an order is issued by His Majesty the Governor to withdraw the person's citizenship. Except if person acquired one of the nationalities of the Member States of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf. Art. 7(1) talks explicitly about female citizens who acquires the citizenship of her foreign spouse.; Person is a naturalised citizen and retrieves his original citizenship without obtaining the prior permission of the Minister of Interior. Except if the person holds one of the nationalities of the Member States of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf. Art. 7(2) talks explicitly about female naturalised citizens who acquired the Bahraini citizenship as a spouse of a male citizen, who retrieves her original citizenship after marriage ties are broken. ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born in Bahrain to a male citizen. The father has to be Bahraini citizen at the time of the child's birth; Person is born in Bahrain to a female citizen, providing that the father was either unknown or the child was not legally connected to the father. The mother has to be Bahraini citizen at the time of the child's birth. ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born in Bahrain to a male citizen. The father has to be Bahraini citizen at the time of the child's birth; Person is born in Bahrain to a female citizen, providing that the father was either unknown or the child was not legally connected to the father. The mother has to be Bahraini citizen at the time of the child's birth. ... No provision ... No provision
